fixes.explanation: Paul says some slanderously claim that we say “Let us do evil that good may result”. Notice the word slanderously. These people are putting words in his mouth. Then Paul says of them, “Their condemnation is deserved!”

Paul asks what the advantage of being a Jew is, and he answers fast: "Much in every way." Right after talking about circumcision being a matter of the heart (Romans 2:29), you might expect him to say there's nothing left. He doesn't say that, friend. He says there's plenty, and he's about to start counting.

Paul quotes the Scriptures: "So that You may be proved right when You speak and victorious when You judge." Two things happen in that line, God speaks and God judges, and He comes out on top both times. Paul had just said, "Let God be true and every man a liar," and this line is his backup. No plot twist, no upset, friend.

Right, because Paul says, "Certainly not!" He's only trying the idea on, and he marks it with "I am speaking in human terms." Then he shuts it down with a question: "In that case, how could God judge the world?"

That's not what the quote says. It says, "All have turned away, they have together become worthless…" Keeping the law doesn't show up in the quote at all. The verse closes with "there is no one who does good, not even one."

The last quote says, "There is no fear of God before their eyes." After the throats, tongues, mouths and feet, this one turns to the eyes. What's missing from that picture is the fear of God. It's the last of the quotes Paul gives.
